title: Digital Assets Regulation in a Shifting Global Landscape | World Economic Forum
gist: A short WEF and BCG report summary argues digital assets are becoming part of financial infrastructure, making regulation a driver of monetary sovereignty, capital flows and sanctions enforcement. It offers a nine-dimension playbook based on 35 jurisdictions and stresses cross-border cooperation; the text is promotional with no data or market calls.

insights.claim: Digital assets are ceasing to be a stand-alone market and are becoming part of mainstream financial infrastructure, and this transition is accelerating.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Frames crypto exposure as an infrastructure/integration trade rather than a speculative niche; watch institutional adoption channels.
insights.quote: Digital assets are moving beyond a stand-alone market and becoming part of the financial infrastructure.

insights.claim: As digital assets integrate into finance, regulation will determine not only market integrity and financial stability but also monetary sovereignty, capital flows, sanctions enforcement and the future competitiveness of financial systems.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Regulatory choices become a macro and geopolitical variable; jurisdictions' stances may redirect capital and market share.

insights.claim: A WEF and Boston Consulting Group report drawing on regulatory developments across 35 jurisdictions identifies nine dimensions policy-makers must consider, including legal certainty, custody, digital money, financial crime, market integrity and infrastructure.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A checklist to benchmark jurisdictions' readiness; gaps in custody or legal certainty flag where institutional entry is hardest.
insights.locator: Developed by the World Economic Forum

insights.claim: The report positions itself as a practical playbook letting jurisdictions at any stage assess risks, sequence priorities and decide where existing rules suffice versus need adaptation, implying regulation need not start from scratch.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
entities: Regulation of Digital Assets in a Shifting Global Landscape
insights.so_what: Suggests incremental adaptation of existing rules is the expected path, favoring gradual rather than abrupt regime change.
insights.locator: The report offers a practical playbook

insights.claim: Regulatory cooperation, common standards and cross-border trust are presented as the route to safe institutional adoption of digital assets while preserving legitimate national choices.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Standard harmonization is a precondition for institutional flows; track international standard-setting as an adoption catalyst.
insights.locator: It also explores how regulatory cooperation

insights.claim: The framing of the shifting global landscape implies divergent national approaches persist, with the report explicitly leaving room for national policy choices alongside shared standards.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Regulatory fragmentation risk remains; cross-jurisdiction arbitrage may persist.
